[quote=the_crystalline_empire;58823060][b]Tactics[/b]

There was much hustle and bustle in the government of Thýven as the invitation to a special summit in Kingsmount was thrown back at them. Of course it provided eager expansionists the opportunity to see potential economic exploits, and political theorists the opportunity to study the full nature of the Albic government.

However, despite the hubbub and madness that stoked the government of Thýven, the crown remained firm, it would attend the meeting and summit with one goal, the goal to ensure a proper power-bloc was formed in order to provide for the common defense. Or as Mij Drs put it frequently [i]Fíjr Pjolés[/i] (For the People). 

Preparations were thus made on Thývens side for the 81-year old monarch to make an appearance as the head of the delegation, both as a show of the supremacy of the ancient monarchy and as a show of Adní given monarchical authority with which the Albic peoples had long abandoned. 

The delegation would arrive in Kingsmount via a simple unmarked white plane, of which the only manner by which might tell that it carried precious treasure aboard was by radio comms. The plane was intentionally chosen as an austerity tactic, perhaps to signify the austerity of the Thýven government against the seemingly bloated Albic government, which is what many in Thýven viewed Albany as, blþa. [/quote]
Rather than a grand and pomp ceremony, however, Minister Ostman would advise the Blythe directorship to receive the Thýven delegation with a simple function at Kingsmount, with Minister Ostman and several of her Radical Party allies simply greeting the esteemed monarch with an exchange of hands before ushering them into the state palace to begin the talks. No reporters would be permitted, with Minister Ostman citing that the summit will necessitate an exchange of geopolitically sensitive information.

As everyone settled down in their seats in the central meeting chamber of Kingsmount Palace, Minister Ostman looked to the service staff as they poured the drinks into each of the dignitaries' cups. The Thrømm received their share first as the guests of honor, then the High Albics, then the Norrics. The drink was a kind of infused spirit, made from apple cider and cinnamon. Apple Pie Moonshine the Thrømm would overhear the Albics call it, though there was no moonshine in it but a cacophany of legal spirits and vodka which helped with its subtle kick. 

Subtle, for its sweet flavor would render its strong profile dangerously subtle to the irresponsible drinker.

"I hope that His Majesty's trip to Kingsmount had been pleasant." Minister Ostman began, taking a sip of the light refreshment as she stared carefully at the Thrømm delegation. "As we've stated in the initial message we presented to the Thrømm adminstration, the Commonwealth does not find itself necessarily aligned with the present geopolitical goals of THEP, but please entrust in me that we did not simply decide to host this summit to reiterate this fact."

Perhaps it was the drinks, perhaps the advice of her own allies, but her words seemed ephemerally gentle and conciliatory for that fleeting moment.

"... Now, as of this moment we are observing foreign actors expanding along the coastlines of the White Straits, Technocratic forces emerging in the far west seeking to weaken their peaceful neighbors, and the east is no better off." The Minister's voice was cool and organized, almost mechanical even as she listed down the present messes of Erene like some ghastly calendar of activities. "The Commonwealth understands, therefore, that isolation is foolishness, and yet we understand that to be associated with too many powers is its own kind of foolishness too. Therefore, let me propose a middle ground, Your Majesty."

The Minister turned to her aide, who would bring up a map of the general area around Elseyr and Vespuria. Prominently, a number of states surrounding High Albany would be encircled, Thýven included.

"Your Majesty." Ostman began. "What do you say we create a new military pact, dedicated towards ensuring our shared dominance of the White Sea?"

*In those distant days, distant nights , from the seas he came, from Chimancu to the far north he came,  with bare feet and nothing but a skirt, Taycanamo was the choosen by gods to rule, choosen by Chilla and Cochanamo to be the first among men.
In 3450 Taycanamo and his subjects  founded Chanchán from adobe, at center of it, the large Chillakóri was constructed, a large temple with adobe walls, while it halls were made with stone and silver , at the centre of such imponent building, Taycanamo received his mandate from Chilla and the divine bless of his lineage*
By far , his most loyal partner was Íchkilla, who bore him Guacrí Càur and Taychár, Guacrí Càur was born on the 44990 cycle (April 952) and Taychár born in the 45035 cycle (September 955).
Guacrí Càur had a powerful body, and was strong, he was a great military leader, who launched expeditions against the Mochykas at east conquering their lands and founding Chimbote at 3470(970) .
at west Taychár allied chief of Ishma tribes, Irûmá, against illapa locals, they emerged victorious, and Piwra was founded as symbol of both people alliance in 3473(973).
And the three pillars of the empire were founded, Chanchán Chansanga, Chimbote the Farsanga and Piwra the Piwrasanga/Ishmasanga, the three parts of empire were founded.
At south, the yungás, a savage people from the south emerged as a power to be cautious with, under leadership of Mìtik led a attack right into the heart of the empire, attacking to destroy Chanchán , Mìtik led a army of 20k men, equiped with clubs and axes, the imperial soldiers were armed withhalberds and slingshots, from the top of the adobe walls, in the towers, in order of protect our impenetrable gates , our men attacked by using slingshots and a Tárbû/"a large mechanism thrower of stones"( interpreted as a early Chimú catapult), which terrified the  yungás, when retreating, surrounded by Guacrí Càur they were , And Mìtik had his head decapitated by Guacrí Càur himself using a halberd
At the 3483 year (983) in the Chillakóri, Chilla appeared for Taycanamo as a silver owl to deliver him a message "My Camácinite son, your time to rule the Camác was thriving and long, brought peace to the land and skies, but now your time has came to pass your crown to the next generation of the silver lineage"
In a celestial voice she said , Taycanamo accepted his fate, and raised his hand, and said in his last words.
"Then let us see who shall be worthy of keeping the silver lineage".
.
.
.
The ceremony was large, Taycanamo mummified in a corner of the Chillakóri throne room in a statue of gold and silver details.
Táycànichilla, where 7 Kurakas and 3 sacerdots would choose the new ruler among the kids of Taycanamo, both heirs, or more , were put in center between the throne, with a silver bow with fire burning on it, the fire was a representation of the eternal rule, if the fire stop burning, no one is  worthy to take place as leader of the silver lineage , but it never stopped burning , the first one to approach was  Guacrí Càur, the throne had a weak light of the moon passing throught the throne room glass dome at the top, weaker than average, then, Tachày moved next to the throne, the moon light shined stronger, illuminating him more, and then the sacerdots affirmed.
"Taychár was choosen , the silver lineage will live, and Taychár will serve as it ruler".
As soon he did down the throne, Taychár had his crown of silver and jewelry, alongside a silver feather on top, in front of him In a small stone table alongside a chicha (corn beevarage), he drank the Chicha, and put the crown on his own head, as symbol of his power, he then said*
"I  , Taychár son of Taycanamo was chosen by the gods to keep the silver lineage, the next leader of humanity, and to bring stability to Camác and the skies"
He swear a oath

Queen Drs would listen intently, her piercing brown eyes staring at the minister as she droned on, after a few moments of silence and a few whispers amongst those staffers on the Thrømm side the queen would speak, her words tight and tinged with nobility, posh yet not prickish.

"It has long been our goal back in Thýven to ensure the strategic White Sea was held strongly against any foreign attacks, given that we own most of the islands in the sea, minus the Austmark, it would be strategic at best to accept this deal, given the fact that it is dangerous for only one nation to hold the full power while the other makes deals behind the back of many to undermine ones power over the sea."

She paused.

"I will accept on behalf of the government, but I must see the details for this alliance and its purposes," she continued as more mutters went among the Thrømm staffers, usually the queen never stepped out of her bounds of smiling and waving and dealing with parliament with a seven foot pole, distance was her name, but it seemed that she had done the unprecedented for her reign thusfar, she had drawn the matter close to her, and closed the need for parliament in the situation. It was a dangerous and calculated move to ensure swift conclusion and not drawn out months of waiting for parliament to make up its mind.

Location: Fort Aegis, Etherniasti High-Security Detention Facility
Date: March 17, 2025  21:00 Hours

[i]INTERROGATION ROOM 03  SUBJECT: PRISONER #217
[/i]
The small, dimly lit room smelled of sweat and iron. Captain Elias Vaelor sat across from Prisoner #217, one of the five captured Sal-Baliz operatives from the intercepted vessel. The prisoners hands were cuffed to the metal table, his face bruised but defiant. The flickering light above cast shadows on his unmoving expression.

Vaelor exhaled through his nose and opened a thick dossier on the table, revealing photos of the missile strike on Port Thriump, the wreckage, the bodies. He let the images linger before flipping to intelligence reports and movement logs showing Sal-Balizs activities leading up to the attack.

"Four hundred dead. Hundreds more injured," Vaelor said calmly, tapping a finger on one of the images. "This is what your country did. This is what youre part of."

The prisoner didnt flinch. "I have nothing to say," he muttered, shifting in his seat.

Vaelor leaned forward, his voice turning ice cold. "Thats fine. I dont need you to talk. But heres the thingyoure in Etherniasti custody, and Etherniasti follows the rules. We treat our prisoners fairly." He let the words settle before lowering his tone. "But United Hydronia? Theyre different. They dont ask politely. They dont care about Geneva or prisoner rights. And they want you. Badly."

The prisoners jaw tightened.

Vaelor continued, his eyes locked onto the man in front of him. "Were at war now. Your government made sure of that. We could keep you here for the rest of your life, let you rot away in a dark cell. Or we could send you to Hydronia. You know what happens there, dont you?"

A flicker of unease crossed the prisoners face, but he stayed silent.

Vaelor stood, pushing the folder aside. "You have a choice. Cooperate with us, tell us what we need to know, and you stay here, treated under Etherniasti law. Stay quiet, and we hand you over to people who wont be as patient."

The prisoner swallowed hard. A bead of sweat rolled down his temple.

Vaelor stepped toward the door, nodding to the guards. "Put him back in his cell. Let him think about it."

As the guards dragged him out, Prisoner #219in the next roomcould be heard shouting in agitation. The idea of United Hydronia's "methods" had already begun to break them.

Etherniasti would get the answers it neededone way or another.

[i]The Reichswehr moved quickly to encircle and cut off the British Republic from the rest of Erene. A no fly zone would be enforced by the F-15 and F-16 fleet accompanied by collaborative combat aircraft and AWACs. The Kaiserliche Marine using its surface attack groups and an array of nuclear submarines as well as UUVs would enforce a total blockade of the island. Nothing would be able to enter or leave the island without facing the arsenal of the Imperial Reichswehr. 

Now that the trap had been sprung, the Luftstreitkrafte would rain down hell on the Bobians. 

In the outskirts of Neudresden, Eisenstadt and Stahlbasin, the well oiled and deadly imperial machine of war would launch into action. F-15s, aerial refuelers and collaborative combat aircraft would take off in rapid succession. As they moved closer to the island they would be joined by the F/A-18Cs aboard the helicopter carrier strike group. The first to breach Bobian airspace would be the CCAs. Using their powerful sensors they would gather information over the battlefields and return it to Kriegskommand maintaining a constant flow of data. At the same time, the electrical warfare apparatus aboard the CCAs would bombard Bobian communications, breaking them down and causing chaos while degrading Bobian coordination. 

F-15s and the kinetic strike collaborative combat aircraft would remain behind in the low threat zone, allowing them to stay out of significant danger while allowing the CCAs to do their work. Once the CCAs, satellites and UAVs had located Bobian military aircraft they would launch into action. At before-visual-range the F-15s would launch AIM-120 AMRAAMs and JTAMs allowing them to destroy Bobian aircraft while out of the visual range of the enemy. CCAs, acting as force multipliers would unleash massive amounts of firepower along with the F-15s. Their newer and more advanced systems would be able to launch AGM-88 HARM missiles which would track the radiation signature of any Bobian aircraft as well as hypersonic glide missiles which could bypass missile defenses at hypersonic speeds. 

Fourth generation aircraft and aerial refuelers would stay well out of the way of Bobian air defenses. They would maintain the logistical function of the air forces with the fourth generation aircraft coordinating strikes for the CCAs as well as maintaining the data links. Aerial refuelers would make sure that the F-15s and CCAs could constantly remain in the sky. AWACs also in this area would track any incoming Bobian aircraft and missiles and relay the information to the CCAs and F-15s for them to destroy. 

The assault of the Kaiserliche Marine would be equally relentless. 

The surface attack groups composed of missile carriers, destroyers and helicopter carriers would launch hundreds of vollies of hypersonic missiles into Bobian territory, attacking warships, ports, and coastal defenses. Hundreds of UUVs would be dispatched into Bobian waters to hunt down their submarines. The UUVs themselves, although cheaper, would be extremely deadly. Equipped with torpedoes they would swarm enemy submarines, each of the drones cheaper than the torpedoes being used on the submarine. On the surface, USVs would launch attacks against Bobian craft, launch NSM Harpoon missiles, and act as decoys to confuse enemy craft. The TKS Seeschlange and TKS Krakenwolf would quickly appear, launch their respective payloads of 154 cruise missiles at the Bobian fleet and quickly submerge.[/i]

Mr. Xavier Almstedt, the incumbent President and CEO of SummitONE, would react positively to the successful negotiation of the contract, and would swiftly send over a massive garrison of 10,000 SummitONE Contractors together with 800 professional military advisors, the majority of them elite stock belonging to the Albic Armed Forces and the State of Norrhollow's elite CAUSE force.

Operations Manager Freya Moran, one of SummitONE's commanders who had been initially intended to serve as the lieutenant to the company's operations in West Shamat, would be swiftly rediverted by Xavier Almstedt to instead take charge of the company's new branch office within the British Republic. 

The bulk of SummitONE's contractors would arrive in the British Republic by Springflame airlifts, though Moran and her command would arrive last by civilian transport escorted by Albic-manufactured Eurofighter Typhoons, which would act as a check on the Reichswehr's intrusion into its airspace. Upon arriving without incident, Moran would moved to take charge of one of the British Republic's aircraft carriers, establishing it as SummitONE's base of operations on the island.

The private force is expected to be augmented by tanks, attack helicopters, missile boats, and loitering munitions over the coming days, with shipments already en route through the White Straits from Stormhaven.

[quote=sultanate_of_orman;58825302][b]Orman Condemns [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation] Terror Campaign as War Escalates[/b]

March 17, 2025  Al-Mahra (Sarmadiah), [nation]Sultanate of Orman[/nation]  As the war between [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation] and the Coalition ([nation]United Hydronia[/nation], [nation]The Crystalline Empire[/nation], [nation]Sherman Tank[/nation], [nation]Italian Dutch[/nation], [nation]Etherniasti[/nation], [nation]Lavinsworth United Islands[/nation], and [nation]Camphill[/nation]) intensifies, shocking reports have emerged confirming that [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation] itself is the terrorist entitynot just a state sponsor of extremism, but the central force behind a brutal campaign of terror.

New intelligence from Coalition sources and independent investigators has revealed that [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation] is directly responsible for orchestrating mass killings, targeting civilians, and destabilizing the region through systematic terror operations. The [nation]Sultanate of Orman[/nation], known for its neutrality, has now been forced to reevaluate its position as global pressure mounts against [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation]s reign of terror.

⸻

[b][nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation]s Reign of Terror[/b]: The Truth Revealed

Investigations confirm that [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation] is not merely funding terrorist groupsit is the terrorist regime itself. The theocracys leadership has been actively ordering massacres, ethnic purges, and attacks on civilian populations across the region. Key findings include:
		State-Orchestrated Genocide  Reports from war-torn areas indicate that [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation]s forces have been deliberately executing civilians, particularly in regions resisting its radical rule.
		Suicide Bombings & Mass Executions  Eyewitness accounts describe systematic bombings of marketplaces, hospitals, and schools, with [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation] clerics justifying the killings as divine acts.
		Foreign Backing for Terror Operations  Evidence suggests that [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation] receives financial and logistical support from external extremist networks, fueling its reign of terror.
		Religious Extremism & Forced Conversions  [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation]s theocratic leadership has imposed a brutal purification doctrine, forcing civilians to either submit to their ideology or face execution.

[b]A Coalition spokesperson declared[/b]:
[nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation] is not a rogue stateit is a terrorist regime in control of an entire nation. Every moment they remain in power, innocent lives are lost. The world cannot stand by as they slaughter entire populations.

⸻

[b]Ormans Response[/b]: Security Measures & Diplomatic Pressure

The Ormani government has responded with shock and outrage at the revelations. While maintaining its historical stance of neutrality, the Sultanate is now under intense pressure to take action. 

[b]The Foreign Ministry of Orman issued the following statement[/b]:

The [nation]Sultanate of Orman[/nation] strongly condemns the systematic terror being waged by [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation]. The targeting of civilians, religious extremism, and mass killings violate all principles of humanity and justice. The international community must unite against this threat.

[b]Orman has taken immediate security measures to prevent any [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation] infiltration[/b]:
		Full Border Closures  All entry points from territories linked to [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation] have been shut down.
		Intelligence Crackdown  Ormani intelligence agencies are working with international partners to identify and dismantle any sleeper cells or radical networks within Orman.
		Financial Sanctions  Ormans banking sector is freezing assets linked to [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation] sympathizers and cutting off any financial transactions that could support the regime.

⸻

[b]Public Outrage in Orman[/b]: Calls for Action Grow

The revelation that [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation] is the terrorist force behind mass atrocities has sent shockwaves across Orman. Public sentiment, once divided, has now shifted overwhelmingly against [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation], with nationwide protests demanding stronger action.
		No Tolerance for Terror Protests  Thousands have taken to the streets in Al-Mahra (Sarmadiah), Adhaniyah, and other cities, calling for a direct response against [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation].
		Clerics & Religious Leaders Speak Out  Prominent Islamic scholars in Orman have denounced [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation]s extremist ideology, declaring it a perversion of faith.
		Business & Trade Pressure  Ormani companies are urging the government to completely sever any economic ties with states suspected of supporting [nation]Sal-Baliz[/nation].

[b]Political analyst Samir Al-Fayez stated[/b]:
Ormans neutrality is being tested like never before. The Sultanate must now decidedoes it remain an observer, or does it take a stand against terror.?

[spoiler= Rising Tides]The hum of aircraft echoed over the choppy waters of Lake Ilinalta as the Diplomatic Forces of Jomsland moved to secure its influence. For decades, the region had been a fragmented mix of independent cities, old alliances, and remnants of past empires. Now, Jomsland was making its move.
On the eastern islands of Duncalder, Jomslands economic outreach had already taken root. Investment in infrastructure, ports, and energy production had made the islands increasingly dependent on Jomslands economy. When local authorities hesitated to sign a formal integration agreement, political pressure mounted.Protests broke out, some spontaneous, others planned.  A referendum was held within months, and the islands voted in favor of full annexation, greatly influenced by Jomsland's diplomatic corps and media.
 The growth was more subdued in the Free City of Sbrozonija.  The city had long prospered as a hub for neutral trade, but its position became vulnerable due to the region's growing volatility. Jomslands intelligence agencies quietly supported pro-integration politicians, while its corporations secured critical sectorsbanking, logistics, and energy. By the time the citys leadership formally requested Jomslands partnership, the Commonwealth already controlled most of its infrastructure. A treaty was signed, preserving Sbrozonijas nominal autonomy while integrating its military and economy into Jomslands sphere. The Commonwealth also intergrated the Duchy of Riconia, located on the northern shores of the lake, into its borders aswell as the territories of Fredericksborg and Wøjågard.
As night fell over Lake Ilinalta, Jomslands navy patrolled its newly expanded waters, its influence now undeniable. The Commonwealth has not only started securing the lakeit had started reshaping the regions future.[/spoiler]

[b]A Normal Day in Government[/b]
The Ministry of Culture office in Kingsmount was like any other government building in the capitalrows of identical desks, the steady hum of bureaucratic machinery, and the slow but methodical procession of paperwork. On the twenty-second floor, in the Department of Esoteric Studies, a small team was assembling yet another report for the Ministry of Security. The request had been routine: a reassessment of unregistered cults and Old Faith remnants, a periodic cataloguing effort to ensure compliance with national secular regulations. These reports were always compiled in cooperation with federal security agencies, ensuring that no organization slipped too far into secrecy or subversion.

The report preparation followed standard procedure. The analysts sifted through registry files, legal records, and past investigations, cross-referencing newly submitted group declarations with the existing database. Most of the report concerned benign organizationshistorical societies that traced their lineage to pre-unification cults, folklore groups that preserved superstitions as cultural heritage, and academic circles that studied arcane symbology with no real belief attached. Others, particularly the esoteric movements, required further scrutiny. There were those who claimed enlightenment through ancient texts, those who gathered under the banner of forgotten deities whose names had long since faded from the public consciousness, and those who sought hidden knowledge in art, poetry, and artifacts from Albanys distant past.

Some groups were purely social, aristocratic gatherings indulging in the aesthetics of the occult without true conviction. Others were fronts for scams, preying on those desperate for purpose or belonging. A smaller but more concerning subset included doomsayers, nationalist cults who wrapped their faith in historical revisionism, and secretive sects that refused government registration, operating at the edges of legal tolerance. Internal Security had flagged several such groups for observation, though no immediate action had been recommendedyet.

As the team compiled the findings, something felt off. One of their colleagues, a quiet but diligent analyst, had been acting strangely over the past few weeks. He was the sort who rarely spoke out of turn, meticulous in his work, yet his behavior had changed. He lingered too long over certain documents, muttered to himself while reading reports, and sometimes left the office for unexplained meetings. No one commented on it. In government work, it was best not to ask too many questions.

The final draft of the report included several case studies. The more academic faiths were left with simple notes of observationhistorical oddities, worth documenting but of no concern. The more elusive sects, those dealing in the arcane or the inexplicable, received stronger scrutiny. There were organizations devoted to entities recorded only in fragmented pre-unification texts, their existence acknowledged yet never explained. Some cults claimed knowledge of government secrets, their beliefs eerily aligning with restricted records from centuries past. A few had evidenceold photographs, faded maps, anomalous artifactsthat, though inconclusive, raised quiet questions.

There were also the disappearances. Over the decades, groups that had grown too large, too organized, had been dismantled, their members scattered or arrested. Officially, they had violated secular laws or threatened government stability. Unofficially, there were always rumorswhispers that some of these groups had uncovered something they were not meant to see, that certain knowledge was not meant to be public. The government had no official stance on the supernatural, yet its reactions were often swift when certain lines were crossed. The analysts wrote these sections with careful neutrality, stating only facts, avoiding speculation.

The final day of review came, and the documents were sent up the chain. The report was finalized, classified, and archived. The team signed off on their work, gathered their notes, and prepared for the next assignment. Except one of them never returned.

The quiet analyst was gone. His desk was cleared out, his records erased. When someone mentioned his name, there was no recognition. The department head, when asked, stated that no such person had ever worked there. Those who had spoken with him only days before found themselves doubting their own memories. A few exchanged uneasy glances, but nothing was said. The report was dug up, reclassified, and sealed under national security directives.

The Ministry of Culture continued its work. The Department of Esoteric Studies moved on to its next assignment. The missing man was not spoken of again.
